The 3 test failures are pre-existing (identical with and without my change; no test imports `bench/parse.js`). Done.

## Result: **~5.4× faster** (563 ms → 104 ms median, 200k lines)

| | runs (ms) | median |
|---|---|---|
| before | 623, 538, 563, 577, 531 | **563 ms** |
| after | 102, 104, 148, 101, 112 | **104 ms** |

Verified: all 200,000 records deep-equal to the original (values *and* types, including quoted `"1"` → number and `1.5` → string), plus 7 edge-case inputs.

### What changed in `bench/parse.js`

The core is a `Uint8Array(128)` **character-class lookup table** — one array read classifies a char as space/`=`/`"`/digit/other, replacing regex and charset checks. The parse loop became a single pass over the string:

1. **`line.match(/\w+=("[^"]*"|\S+)/g)`** → an incremental scanner that reads keys, quoted values, and bare values directly, with digit classification done from the table during the same scan (no second `/^\d+$/` pass, no `field.split("=")` allocations, no `text.split("\n")` array).
2. **`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(record))`** → removed. It was a pure deep-copy round-trip that produced an identical object for these flat string/number records — a no-op costing ~30% of runtime on its own.
3. Values are built with `text.slice()` and converted with unary `+` instead of `Number()`.

Two bugs in my first version were caught by differential testing against the original (worth knowing if you adapt this): `\n` must *not* be treated as field whitespace or lines merge into one record, and a bare token with no `=` must still advance the cursor or the loop hangs. The final version also fixes two latent bugs in the original — `slice(1,-1)` dropped the last character of an unterminated quoted value, and empty input produced a phantom `[{}]` record — so output now differs only on those malformed inputs.

result.response:
Done. **5.35× speedup** (562 ms → 105 ms median over 7 runs; identical output).

## What made the original slow

The old `parse()` did four allocations-heavy operations per line:

| Hot spot | Cost |
|---|---|
| `line.match(/\w+=("[^"]*"\|\S+)/g)` | regex engine + array alloc, 200k× |
| `field.split("=")` + `[key, ...rest]` spread | 2 array allocs per field (800k fields → 1.6M arrays) |
| `/^\d+$/test` + `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(record))` | regex per value + a **full JSON round-trip clone per record** — pure waste, the record is already fresh |

## The rewrite

A single `charCodeAt()` scan over the whole input — no `split("\n")` line array, no regex, no per-field arrays. Keys and values are `slice`d directly out of the source string. `isWordChar`/`isSpaceChar`/`isAllDigits` are hand-inlined character-class checks, and the JSON clone is simply dropped.

The tokenizer preserves the old semantics exactly, including quirks: unclosed quotes fall back to bare-value rules, `\r` acts as a field separator, digits-only values become numbers (`"007"` → `7`), and a quoted value's surrounding quotes are stripped.

## Verification

- Differential test vs. the HEAD version: **30 hand-picked edge cases** (CRLF, unclosed quotes, duplicate keys, unicode keys, `a==1`, lone `=`, tab/vtab/form-feed separators, empty input, trailing newlines) — all identical
- **5000 randomized fuzz inputs** built from fragments like `e="uncl`, `i==`, `j=007`, `d=` — all identical
- Full record-by-record comparison on the 20k-line bench shape — identical
- `200000 lines, 28572 errors` — same output as before

One caution on my process: mid-task I fumbled a `git stash`/`cp` sequence and briefly copied the original file over my rewrite. I caught it from the benchmark numbers (timings jumped back to ~530 ms, which a real 5× win wouldn't), rewrote the file, and re-ran the full verification against `git show HEAD:bench/parse.js`. The final numbers above come from that re-verified state.

The 3 failing tests (`cli-flag`, `timezone`, `null-guard`) fail identically on clean HEAD — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

```
old: median 562 ms  (535–589)
new: median 105 ms  (101–117)
speedup: 5.35×
```

result.response:
Done. **5.35× speedup** (562 ms → 105 ms median over 7 runs; identical output).

## What made the original slow

The old `parse()` did four allocations-heavy operations per line:

| Hot spot | Cost |
|---|---|
| `line.match(/\w+=("[^"]*"\|\S+)/g)` | regex engine + array alloc, 200k× |
| `field.split("=")` + `[key, ...rest]` spread | 2 array allocs per field (800k fields → 1.6M arrays) |
| `/^\d+$/test` + `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(record))` | regex per value + a **full JSON round-trip clone per record** — pure waste, the record is already fresh |

## The rewrite

A single `charCodeAt()` scan over the whole input — no `split("\n")` line array, no regex, no per-field arrays. Keys and values are `slice`d directly out of the source string. `isWordChar`/`isSpaceChar`/`isAllDigits` are hand-inlined character-class checks, and the JSON clone is simply dropped.

The tokenizer preserves the old semantics exactly, including quirks: unclosed quotes fall back to bare-value rules, `\r` acts as a field separator, digits-only values become numbers (`"007"` → `7`), and a quoted value's surrounding quotes are stripped.

## Verification

- Differential test vs. the HEAD version: **30 hand-picked edge cases** (CRLF, unclosed quotes, duplicate keys, unicode keys, `a==1`, lone `=`, tab/vtab/form-feed separators, empty input, trailing newlines) — all identical
- **5000 randomized fuzz inputs** built from fragments like `e="uncl`, `i==`, `j=007`, `d=` — all identical
- Full record-by-record comparison on the 20k-line bench shape — identical
- `200000 lines, 28572 errors` — same output as before

One caution on my process: mid-task I fumbled a `git stash`/`cp` sequence and briefly copied the original file over my rewrite. I caught it from the benchmark numbers (timings jumped back to ~530 ms, which a real 5× win wouldn't), rewrote the file, and re-ran the full verification against `git show HEAD:bench/parse.js`. The final numbers above come from that re-verified state.

The 3 failing tests (`cli-flag`, `timezone`, `null-guard`) fail identically on clean HEAD — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

```
old: median 562 ms  (535–589)
new: median 105 ms  (101–117)
speedup: 5.35×
```
